chunks: Everything in this book that is narrated from Yunus ibn 'Ammar has been transmitted by me from my father - may Allah have mercy on him - from Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Malik ibn 'Atiyyah, from Abu Al-Hasan Yunus ibn 'Ammar ibn Al-Fayd Al-Sayrafi Al-Taghlibi Al-Kufi, who was the brother of Ishaq ibn 'Ammar.

key_terms.أَحْمَدُ بْنُ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.الصَّيْرَفِيُّ: Al-Sayrafi, a nisba indicating profession or origin
key_terms.الْحَسَنُ بْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Sa'd ibn Abdullah, a key narrator in the chain
key_terms.مَالِكُ بْنُ عَطِيَّةَ: Malik ibn 'Atiyyah, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.يُونُسَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ: Yunus ibn 'Ammar, a prominent early Shia narrator

ai.seo_question: How is the transmission chain for Yun ibn 'Ammar's narrations structured in Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih?
ai.summary: This passage establishes the specific *isnad* (transmission chain) used by Shaykh al-Saduq for all narrations attributed to Yunus ibn 'Ammar, ensuring consistency in his compilation of *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih*. By tracing the lineage from his father through prominent Kufan scholars like Ahmad ibn Abi 'Abdillah and al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, al-Saduq highlights the reliability and scholarly pedigree of Yunus, a key figure in early Shia hadith transmission. This methodological note underscores the importance of chain verification in Shia jurisprudence to authenticate the Imam's teachings.
